scope: Proposition 6.7 (A witness near every center) of the manuscript “Rigidity of Smooth Billiards with a Continuous Caustic Collar” (preprints/Rigidity-of-Smooth-Billiards-with-a-Continuous-Caustic-Collar-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 147 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 0fefc18481d52acb), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 65. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Suppose, for all sufficiently small δs, that δs max ℑs=H−δs M(s) ≤ C 1 + log(1/δs) A for some fixed C, A. Then there are constants L, C1, C2, c∗ > 0 such that for every sufficiently large k = log(1/d) and every real center x0, there is a point s with |ℜs − x0| ≤ Lδs, k − C1 log k ≤ log(1/δs) ≤ k + C2, δsM(s) ≥ c∗.
